clue.text: New tour price takes in old island

indicators.note: takes in means the shuffled letters swallow another piece inside them
new suggests the letters of tour price are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh holiday price now includes a trip to some historic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TOUR PRICE into PUERTRICO's frame, and 'takes in' puts O (old) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerto Rico is a Caribbean island territory of the United States, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Ostentation of Roman general without the old backing

indicators.note: without tells us some letters are dropped from the general's name

parts.note: Pompey the Great was a general of the late Roman Republic

indicators.note: backing means the archaic word is read in reverse order

parts.note: ye is the old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: A Roman commander's showiness, minus the old-fashioned support he once had.
explanation.walkthrough: Pompey was Julius Caesar's rival. 'backing' gives EY, which 'without' strips from his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is showy splendour and ceremonial display, a direct synonym for ostentation.

clue.text: Alexander Selkirk's language

indicators.note: the possessive here signals that the name holds the answer inside its letters

explanation.surface: A question about what the castaway Alexander Selkirk spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across alexandER SElkirk. Selkirk, the model for Robinson Crusoe, was a Scot, and Erse is a name for Scottish Gaelic, so the clue is nicely apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland, so it is a kind of language.

clue.text: Women try out fine new book

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are given a fresh order

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade and general abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A group of women are invited to sample a fine newly published book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' shuffles WOMEN TRY OUT together with F (fine).
explanation.definitionFit: Twentyfourmo is a printing term for a book size made by folding each sheet into twenty-four leaves.

clue.text: Steps taken to give Republican the lead in shady area?

indicators.note: to give, with the lead, tells us one letter is shifted to the front
the lead means the front position, where the letter is moved to

parts.note: an umbra is the region of full shadow, as in an eclipse

explanation.surface: Someone is dancing their way into the shade so a Republican can lead.
explanation.walkthrough: UMBRA's R is moved from fourth place to the front, giving RUMBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, so it is a set of steps danced together.

clue.text: Creepy type, wanting coin, taking money at first from bar

parts.note: a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: taking, with from, tells us a letter is removed from the bar word
from marks the word that loses the letter

parts.note: to impede is to bar or obstruct

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of money

explanation.surface: A creepy character, short of cash, starts lifting money from a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link meaning needing. 'taking ... from' removes M (the first letter of money) from IMPEDE, leaving IPEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a many-legged arthropod, a creepy-crawly, so a creepy type in a playful sense.

clue.text: Houdon's Voltaire found in police raid

definitions.meaning: the sculptor Jean-Antoine Houdon made a famous head-and-shoulders sculpture of Voltaire
a raid by police on premises, often for drugs

explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders, and also slang for a police raid.

clue.text: Current trap in a French exam lacking novelty

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: in means the following pieces go inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A student's French exam answer is a trap that lacks any freshness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unoriginal is derivative and copied, so it lacks novelty.

clue.text: Revolutionary book on heavens kept in stock

indicators.note: kept in means the following pieces are placed inside the stock word

parts.note: stock, as in a stock phrase, means trite or hackneyed

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the book comes before the heavens

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a book of the Bible
the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: A radical's book about the heavens is kept in a shop's stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trotskyite is a follower of Leon Trotsky, a revolutionary Marxist.

clue.text: Intellectual dog owner's inclination

parts.note: a dog's owner is its master
a mind to do something is an inclination towards it

explanation.surface: A clever person reflects on what a dog's owner feels like doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastermind is a person of great intellect, so an intellectual in the noun sense.

clue.text: Sickly sentiment about unknown Maltese island

indicators.note: about means the sentiment word goes round the unknown

parts.note: goo is cloying, sentimental gush
Z is one of the algebraic unknowns x, y and z

explanation.surface: Gushing feelings over a mysterious island in the Maltese group.
explanation.definitionFit: Gozo is the second-largest island of the Maltese archipelago, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Take the initiative, beginning to check every drink

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of check is used

parts.note: every drink can be all the shots, shots being small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: A person seizing control starts by checking every drink in the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To call the shots is an idiom for being in charge and making the decisions.

clue.text: One hurries back with different-sounding instrument

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: darts means hurries or dashes
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: sounding says the next piece is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: various means different or diverse

explanation.surface: Someone rushes back holding an instrument with an unusual tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DARTS into STRAD; 'different-sounding' gives VARIUS, said like various.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius is a violin or other string instrument made by Antonio Stradivari.

clue.text: Expel policeman's son law enforcers arrested

parts.note: a DI is a detective inspector, so DI's is the policeman's

indicators.note: arrested means the law enforcers hold the son inside them

parts.note: posses are bands of men gathered by a sheriff to enforce the law
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A policeman's son is arrested by law enforcers and thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispossess is to deprive someone of property, especially by ejecting them from it.

clue.text: Person with pull contributing to various changes?

definitions.text: Person with pull contributing to various changes?

parts.words: Person with pull contributing to various changes?
parts.note: reads like an influential reformer, but the pull is on a rope and the changes are the sequences rung on church bells

explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer pulls a rope to sound a bell, and change-ringing rings bells in varied orders called changes.

clue.text: Unusually fine invention — beyond description

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of fine appear in an odd order

parts.note: a fable is an invented story

explanation.surface: An unusually fine creation is praised as indescribable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffable means too great or extreme to be expressed in words.

clue.text: Winter transport builder and butcher talked of

indicators.note: talked of says the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: Bob the Builder is a children's TV character, and to butcher is to slay

explanation.surface: A builder and a butcher discuss how to get around in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: BOB plus SLAY, spoken, gives the sound of the answer. Bob the Builder is a British children's animated series.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobsleigh is a racing sled used on ice, so a form of winter transport.

clue.text: Flashy hotel ultimately well-ventilated

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of hotel

parts.note: a well-ventilated room is airy

explanation.surface: A showy hotel that turns out to be draughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairy is British slang for vulgarly showy or flashy, often loud in manner too.

clue.text: French city importing the Italian dish

indicators.note: importing means the city takes in the other piece

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-western France
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: A French city imports a dish from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is a rice dish cooked in stock with spices, also spelt pilaf.

clue.text: Conductor finally turned over extremely succulent fruit

indicators.note: finally turned over means the conductor's name has its last pair of letters swapped round

parts.note: Sir Thomas Beecham was a celebrated English conductor

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of succulent

explanation.surface: A conductor's last act is to turn over some very juicy fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally turned over' swaps BEECHAM's last two letters to make BEECHMA; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of succulent.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech mast is the collective name for the nuts that fall from beech trees, their fruit.

clue.text: One whose study is of earthshaking significance

definitions.text: One whose study is of earthshaking significance

parts.words: One whose study is of earthshaking significance
parts.note: reads as a scholar of huge importance, but literally describes someone who studies the shaking of the earth

explanation.definitionFit: A seismologist studies earthquakes, which shake the earth.

clue.text: Diver in church land using river not lake

indicators.note: using, with not, tells us one letter replaces another
not marks the letter being replaced in the church land

parts.note: glebe is land granted to a parish priest as part of his benefice
L is the map abbreviation for lake
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A diver on church land prefers the river to the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In GLEBE the L (lake) is swapped for R (river).
explanation.definitionFit: The grebe is a water bird that dives for its food, so it is a diver.

clue.text: Very big see where Ibsen lived under another name

definitions.text: where Ibsen lived under another name

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A grand see, or bishopric, where the playwright Ibsen lived incognito.
explanation.walkthrough: Oslo was called Christiania while Ibsen lived there, hence 'under another name'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital was named Christiania in Ibsen's time, so it is the city under its later name.

clue.text: Australian redhead's very cold

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang a red-haired person is ironically called by a colour word
skin turns that colour from extreme cold

explanation.definitionFit: Blue is Australian slang for a redhead, and describes skin or a person that is very cold.

clue.text: Border on which we're ill at ease

definitions.text: on which we're ill at ease
definitions.meaning: being nervous is being on this

explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a border, and to be on edge is to be nervous or tense.

clue.text: Evil action by prisoners starts to upset local deputy

parts.note: a vice is wicked or immoral conduct
cons is short for convicts

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Wickedness among inmates begins to disturb the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-consul acts as deputy to a consul, a diplomatic official abroad.

clue.text: Lively appearance of Saint Paul

parts.note: Paul Pry is a nosy busybody from an 1825 comedy, a stock crossword link

explanation.surface: Saint Paul makes an energetic appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance of' is a link. Paul Pry was the meddling title character of John Poole's play, so Paul leads to PRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means nimble and active, especially of an older person, so it is a synonym of lively.

clue.text: The total covers about sixty

indicators.note: covers means the outer pieces go round the word for about

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a score is a total of points

explanation.surface: The total takes in roughly sixty.
explanation.walkthrough: The total here is a noun for a score in a game, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Threescore is three times twenty, an old way of saying sixty.
